raw_response:
I am 55 this year, and I have farmed this land a long time. On my 13.1 mu, I still do wheat and maize in rotation. That is the safest way for me. Wheat gives me one harvest, maize gives me the next, and if one season is not so smooth, at least I still have the other. I only have two people in the house, so I cannot make things too complicated. I will follow the usual local timing. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer at sowing, then add some urea at jointing if the crop stand looks decent. Wheat needs water, so with the well I will irrigate around the key stages, but not too many times because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest, the time is tight, so for maize I will not do heavy tillage. I will clear the field quickly, sow fast, and use a simpler fertilizer plan. I do not like cutting fertilizer too much, because if the crop turns yellow later, yield drops hard. But I also will not push too much, because cash is not loose and every extra bag costs money. If pests or weeds show up, I will spray, otherwise I do not spend first.
